intended_object: The supernatural (Steinitz) index [G:H] of a closed subgroup H of a profinite group G. It is the lcm, over all open normal subgroups U, of the finite indices [G/U : HU/U]. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module documentation.
explanation: The body takes the supremum over U : OpenNormalSubgroup G of the index of the image of H in G/U, and that image is HU/U. In `Supernatural` (Multiplicative (Nat.Primes → ℕ∞)), the order is pointwise on prime exponents, and ofPNat m ≤ ofPNat n holds exactly when m ∣ n. So the supremum is the lcm, which is exactly the standard definition in Serre and in Ribes–Zalesskii. The finite-index instance holds because open subgroups of compact groups have finite index. Degenerate cases behave correctly: the library proves that the trivial subgroup has index equal to the supernatural order, that G itself has index 1, and that the index reverses inclusion. The setting, closed subgroups of profinite groups, is the standard one. Mathlib has no supernatural numbers.
